rules.title: let-else evaluates scrutinee, tests pattern, binds on match else runs diverging block
rules.statement: `let PAT = EXPR else { BLOCK }` evaluates EXPR once, tests it against PAT; on match the pattern's bindings enter the enclosing scope and control continues; on mismatch BLOCK runs. BLOCK must diverge: if it does not terminate, control is unreachable.

rules.title: Wildcard/binding let-else pattern always matches
rules.statement: When PAT is a wildcard or a bare binding (not `_`), the pattern is irrefutable: it always matches and binds the scrutinee value; the else block is unreachable.

rules.title: Enum variant pattern in let-else is refutable on discriminant
rules.statement: For an enum scrutinee, a `Variant`/`VariantData` pattern matches iff the scrutinee's discriminant equals the pattern variant's discriminant; otherwise the else block runs. A C-like (all-nullary) enum scrutinee is its own discriminant value.

rules.title: Or-pattern in let-else matches any alternative
rules.statement: `let A(x) | B(x) = v else …` matches iff the scrutinee discriminant equals any alternative's discriminant (logical OR of per-alt tests). All alternatives must bind the same names at the same payload layout; bindings are extracted using the first alternative's payload.

rules.title: Literal/bool/range pattern in let-else is refutable
rules.statement: For a non-enum integer scrutinee, an `Int` or `Bool` pattern matches iff the scrutinee equals the literal; a `Range` pattern (`lo..=hi`) matches iff `lo <= scrut <= hi` (signed). On mismatch the else block runs.

rules.title: Tuple pattern in let-else is irrefutable
rules.statement: A tuple pattern in let-else is always irrefutable: it unconditionally matches and binds each non-`_` element field to the corresponding scrutinee tuple element.

rules.title: let-else auto-derefs reference scrutinee for enum patterns
rules.statement: When the scrutinee has type `&Enum`, `&mut Enum`, or `*Enum`, the enum variant pattern is tested against the referenced enum (match-ergonomics auto-deref), so `let Some(v) = &opt else …` behaves like a by-value match.

rules.title: Refutable sub-patterns in let-else add value guards
rules.statement: A refutable inner sub-pattern (e.g. `let Some(1) = … else`) lowers to a guard test on the bound payload after the variant discriminant matches; if any guard fails the else block runs. The match succeeds only when the discriminant test and all guards hold.
